q: 1. A stair should not have pitch more than
explain: For comfort and safety, the pitch (angle of inclination) of a standard staircase should generally be between 25° and 40°. Anything steeper becomes difficult and dangerous to climb.

q: 2. When two or more individual column footings are joined by a beam, it is called ........
explain: A strap footing consists of two isolated footings connected by a rigid 'strap' beam to transfer the eccentric load of one footing to the other.

q: 3. The maximum thickness of door shutters provided in door in
explain: Standard commercial and residential door shutters are typically manufactured in thicknesses around 38 mm.

q: 4. Door type without importance
explain: Battened and ledged doors are the simplest and cheapest type, used for low-importance applications like sheds or toilets.

q: 5. In public buildings the minimum tread width of stair case should be
explain: For safety and ease of use in public spaces, codes require a minimum tread width of 30 cm.

q: 6. The minimum width of a stair in a residential building is
explain: Building codes generally specify a minimum width of 80 cm to 90 cm for residential stairs to allow for safe passage and the movement of furniture.

q: 7. A level platform at the top or bottom of a flight between the floors is known as ..........
explain: A landing provides a place to rest or change direction in a staircase.

q: 8. The opening left in flat roofs for lightings purposes is called
explain: A skylight is an opening in a roof covered with glass or plastic to admit natural light.

q: 9. Spiral stair is used when ..........
options: architectural appearance is to be improved
the cost of the stair is to be minimized
explain: Spiral stairs are circular in plan and are highly efficient in saving floor space.

q: 10. A stair which changes its direction by 180° is ..........
explain: A half-turn stair (like dog-legged or open newel) reverses direction by 180 degrees.

q: 11. When stone slabs are used for risers and treads they are connected by ..........
explain: Stone steps are typically either solid masonry or built as independent slabs supported by walls; they are generally not connected by dowels or scotia in standard construction.

q: 12. The horizontal wooden member at the apex of the roof supporting the common rafter is known as ..........
explain: The ridge piece (or ridge board) is the horizontal timber at the very peak of the roof where the upper ends of rafters are fixed.

q: 13. The horizontal member forming the bottom of the frame is called as
explain: The sill is the lowest horizontal part of the window or door frame, designed to shed water away from the opening.

q: 14. When both the flights in a stair run at right angles to each other, then that stair is classified as
explain: A quarter-turn stair changes direction by 90 degrees, usually at a landing.

q: 15. The horizontal members of the frame which divides the window horizontally is ..........
explain: A transom is the horizontal member of a frame that separates a door from a window above it or divides a window horizontally.

q: 16. In the battened and ledged door, the horizontal wooden boards holding the battens together are called ..........
explain: Ledges are the horizontal wooden members to which the vertical battens are secured.

q: 17. The inclined wooden boards which provide additional strength to battens in the battened and ledged door are called ..........
explain: Braces are diagonal members used between ledges to prevent the door from sagging (making it a 'Battened, Ledged, and Braced' door).

q: 18. The type of door used when good lighting is to be permitted into the room ..........
explain: Sash doors (or glazed doors) contain glass panels to allow light transmission while providing a closure.

q: 19. The short piece of timber bolted to the rafters of a roof truss fixing the purlins in position are named as
explain: Cleats are small blocks used to prevent purlins from sliding or tilting on the rafters.

q: 20. The timber sections of width more than 5 cm and thickness less than 5 cm are known as ..........
explain: Scantlings refer to timber cut to standard sizes with specific dimensions; usually, they are smaller pieces of wood.

q: 21. A vertical member supporting the hand rail is known as
explain: Balusters are the smaller vertical members that support the handrail and fill the space between the tread and the rail.

q: 22. In domestic buildings, the sufficient widths of the stair is about
explain: For residential or domestic buildings, a width of 0.9m (approx. 3 feet) is considered sufficient for comfortable movement.

q: 23. A stair which changes its direction by 180° is
explain: Half-turn stairs, such as dog-legged stairs, involve two flights that reverse direction by 180 degrees.

q: 24. How many treads would be there in a straight stair connecting two floors with height difference of 3.6 m? The rise is 15 cm.
explain: Total risers = 360/15 = 24. Since treads = Risers - 1 for a single flight, the answer is 23.

q: 25. The horizontal wooden or steel members which support the common rafter in a truss are called
explain: Purlins are horizontal members spanning between trusses to support the rafters or roofing sheets.

q: 26. Joining two wooden members at an angle is known as
explain: Mitring is the process of joining two pieces of wood at an angle, usually 45 degrees, to form a corner.

q: 27. The depth of jamb is ..........
explain: The depth or thickness of the jamb for a standard door frame generally matches the width, falling in the range of 76 mm to 114 mm.

q: 28. The under surface of a stair is known as ..........
explain: The soffit refers to the visible underside of any structural element, including the underside of a staircase.

q: 29. A horizontal member of stone, concrete or wood provided to give support for the vertical member of a wooden window, is called ..........
explain: The sill is the horizontal bottom member of a window frame that sheds water away from the wall.

q: 30. A series of steps without any platform, break or landing in their direction, is called ..........
explain: A flight is an uninterrupted series of steps between floors or landings.

q: 31. In designing a stair, the product of going (in cm) and twice the rise (in cm) should be equal ..........
explain: Another empirical rule for comfortable stairs is that Tread * Riser should be approximately 400 to 450 cm².

q: 32. In a sloping roof, the inclined wooden members laid from the ridge to the eaves known as ..........
explain: Common rafters extend from the ridge to the eaves and provide the main support for the roof covering.

q: 33. A pitched roof in which rafters slope to one side only is called ..........
explain: A lean-to roof (also known as a pent or shed roof) consists of a single sloping surface, usually attached to a taller wall.

q: 34. The type of truss commonly used for spans varying from 5 to 9 meter is ..........
explain: A King Post truss utilizes a single central vertical post and is most economical for spans in the range of 5 to 9 meters.

q: 35. The process of filling up all nail holes, cracks etc. with putty is known as ..........
explain: Stopping involves using putty or wood filler to smooth out surface imperfections before painting.

q: 36. A truss having upper and lower pitch, and made by combining king and queen post trusses, also used as a roof, is known as ...........
explain: A Mansard truss provides two different slopes on the same side, often utilized to create habitable attic space.

q: 37. The short piece of timber bolted to the rafters of a roof truss fixing the purlin in position are named as ...........
explain: Cleats are small blocks of wood or steel angles fixed to the principal rafters to prevent the purlins from sliding down.

q: 38. Screws for wood work as specified by ...........
explain: Wood screws are commercially classified by their length and their 'gauge' (diameter of the shank).
